title: LibreOffice Calc vs Excel: Which Should You Use?
dek: LibreOffice Calc is a free, open-source desktop spreadsheet; Excel is the paid industry standard with deeper features. Calc covers everyday work at no cost, Excel wins on power and compatibility. Here is how they compare.

seo.metaTitle: LibreOffice Calc vs Excel: Which to Use?
seo.metaDescription: LibreOffice Calc vs Excel compared: a free open-source spreadsheet versus the paid standard. Cost, features, .xlsx compatibility, and who each is for.

richText: LibreOffice Calc and Microsoft Excel do the same core job — rows, columns, and formulas — but they sit at opposite ends of the price and power scale. Calc is free and open-source; Excel is a paid subscription and the standard most workplaces run on. The right pick depends on your budget, the features you actually need, and how often you swap files with Excel users.

body.caption: LibreOffice Calc vs Excel at a glance

richText: Choose Excel when you need the deepest features or when compatibility is non-negotiable. Its advanced tools — Power Query, richer charting, and the widest set of functions — are ahead of Calc, and it stays fast with very large datasets. If your workplace or clients send complex .xlsx files with macros, Excel opens them exactly as intended, every time.

Choose LibreOffice Calc when you want a capable spreadsheet without paying anything. It installs on Windows, Mac, and Linux, needs no account, and works fully offline. body.richText: The main catch is compatibility. Calc opens and saves .xlsx files, but very complex Excel macros, advanced formatting, or specialized features may not carry over perfectly. If you exchange heavy Excel files daily, test a few before committing.

richText: For most people, the choice comes down to files. If you rarely share spreadsheets, or share simple ones, Calc's .xlsx support is more than enough and you save the subscription cost. If you live in a world of complex, macro-heavy Excel files that must look identical for everyone, Excel is the safer choice.

items: LibreOffice Calc is not ideal for teams that depend on advanced Excel-only features or need guaranteed formatting fidelity with complex .xlsx files.

items.question: Is LibreOffice Calc as good as Excel?
items.answerRichText: For everyday work — budgets, lists, calculations, common formulas — it is very close, and it is free. Excel pulls ahead on advanced features like Power Query, richer charts, very large datasets, and perfect compatibility with complex .xlsx files.

items.question: Can LibreOffice Calc open Excel files?
items.answerRichText: Yes. Calc opens and saves .xlsx files, so you can work with Excel documents. Simple files transfer perfectly; very complex macros or advanced formatting may not carry over exactly, so test important files first.

items.question: Is LibreOffice really free?
items.answerRichText: Yes. LibreOffice is free and open-source, with no account required and no subscription. It is funded by a non-profit foundation and community, which is why there is no cost to download or use it.
